experiments.title: Simple pendulum
experiments.summary: Estimate gravitational acceleration from the swing period and the string length.

inputs.label: Pendulum length L
inputs.hint: Measure from the pivot to the centre of the phone.

steps.title: Build the pendulum
steps.text: Fasten the phone securely in a bag or cloth sling hanging from a string, 0.5 to 2 m long. Make sure it cannot fall or hit anything.

steps.title: Orient the phone
steps.text: Hang it with the screen facing you and swing it left and right across your view. This points the phone's X axis along the swing, which is the axis PocketLab analyses.

steps.title: Swing gently
steps.text: Pull it aside by less than 15 degrees (about 25 cm per metre of string), release without pushing, and avoid twisting.

experiments.recordHint: Press Start, then release the pendulum. Let it swing for at least 12 seconds. It stops by itself after 30 seconds.

experiments.title: Magnetic field exploration
experiments.summary: Measure the magnetic field strength and watch it change near a magnet.

steps.title: Find a magnet
steps.text: A fridge magnet or a speaker magnet works. Keep it at least 50 cm from the phone until you are told to bring it closer.

steps.title: Find the sensor
steps.text: The magnetometer is usually near the top edge of the phone. Phones differ, so move the magnet slowly around that area.

experiments.recordHint: Press Start. Keep the magnet far away for the first 5 seconds (the baseline), then bring it slowly toward the phone and away again.

experiments.title: Light intensity
experiments.summary: Record illuminance and compare it with typical lighting levels.

references.label: Very bright indoor light or window

steps.title: Choose a spot
steps.text: Place the phone flat where you want to measure, screen up. Do not cover the sensor, which is usually next to the front camera.

steps.title: Keep conditions steady
steps.text: Avoid moving shadows and keep your body from blocking the light.

experiments.recordHint: Press Start and keep the phone still for at least 5 seconds.

experiments.title: Relative height
experiments.summary: Estimate a change in height from the change in air pressure.

inputs.label: Known height change (optional)
inputs.hint: Positive if you go up. One building floor is about 3 m.

inputs.label: Your latitude (optional)
inputs.hint: For altitude above sea level. Find it in any maps app, for example 23.78. Needs internet; leave empty to skip.

inputs.label: Your longitude (optional)
inputs.hint: For example 90.40. Enter both coordinates or neither.

steps.title: Pick two levels
steps.text: Choose two places at different heights, ideally several floors (10 m or more) apart. A bigger difference gives a more reliable result.

steps.title: Work quickly
steps.text: Weather changes also shift the pressure, so do the whole run within a few minutes.

steps.title: Optional: altitude above sea level
steps.text: If you enter your latitude and longitude, PocketLab asks a free weather service (Open-Meteo) for today's sea-level pressure and also reports your altitude above sea level. Only these two numbers are sent, nothing else.

experiments.recordHint: Press Start and hold still for the first 6 seconds. Move to the other level, then hold still for the last 6 seconds before pressing Stop.
